result:
# REJECT

The piece explains connectomics well and then fails to defend the thing it's actually about. A null result is presented, a consolation claim is substituted for it, and the second half wanders off into other people's projects. Fixable, but not as-is.

---

## Where I got lost

**No scale for the headline number.** "the frozen pipeline predicted correctly about fifty-six percent of the time" — I have no idea whether that's impressive or trivial. Home-field advantage alone lands in the mid-50s. The only reference point offered is the piece's own baseline, which is circular.

**The input encoding is a black box at the exact moment I need it.** "bet three sixty fly encodes pregame measurements as patterns of stimulation along those pathways" — which measurements, mapped by what rule, to which neurons? "an engineered version of presenting something sweet or something bitter" is an image, not a method. This is the hinge of the whole project and it's one sentence of metaphor.

**"The response is read out from selected neurons after the circuit settles."** Selected how? If selected by predictive performance, that's a leakage path — and the script has already shown it's nervous about leakage ("neither stimulus presupposes which team will win"). One unexamined word carrying enormous weight.

**No stakes up top.** Nine paragraphs in before anything suggests why I should care. The closest thing — "Working with the fly now is preparation for asking sharper questions when those larger, more thoroughly measured circuits arrive" — arrives in the last third.

## Unexplained references

**bet365 is the biggest orientation failure in the script.** I'm never told who they are, why a company with that name is doing connectomics, or — critically — that a gambling company has a direct commercial interest in a baseball prediction result. That omission is conspicuous rather than neutral.

Related and specific to narration: read aloud, "bet three sixty five" and "bet three sixty fly" are nearly the same sound. I spent the first minute unsure whether they were two things or one.

**DOOMFLY** arrives as "a project like DOOMFLY" — *like* implies a category I'm already in. I'm not.

**The JavaScript fly animations** are described as though I've seen them. I haven't.

**FlyVis, FlyBody, Fish2, ZAPBench, MICrONS** in rapid succession. Each gets a clause; none gets a reason to be in this story.

Unverifiable specifics (neuron counts, synapse counts, release and publication dates, the half-billion-synapse mouse volume) are asserted without sourcing. I can't evaluate them and the script doesn't help me.

## Smug or performative language

The JavaScript paragraph is the worst stretch — it attacks an opponent I've never seen and substitutes aphorism for argument:

> "The visual appearance of neural control does not establish neural control."

> "That is the difference between illustration and experiment."

Both are true and neither is doing work here. Punching down at unnamed hobbyist animations is a strange use of a paragraph when the project's own result is parity with a baseline.

> "Two opportunities, translated into a language the circuit's own wiring can carry."

Floats free of anything technical. It sounds like a conclusion to an explanation that didn't happen.

## Condescension and audience fit

These two sit three paragraphs apart and describe different viewers:

> "Before that sentence makes any sense, you need one piece of biology."

> "If you work with large language models, you already have an intuition for what makes this strange."

The first tells me I'm not equipped to follow the sentence I just heard — and concedes the opening paragraph didn't land. The second assumes I know transformer architecture. Add "If you work with embeddings, the shape of this will be familiar" and the script is addressing a working ML engineer who needs the definition of a connectome. Pick one viewer.

## Coherence as a story

The spine breaks at the result. Up to "The circuit did not beat it," this is a clean setup–method–result narrative. After it, the subject changes six times — DOOMFLY, closed loops, FlyVis, FlyBody, mushroom-body learning, zebrafish, MICrONS — and bet365fly appears in the back half mostly as the thing that *hasn't* done something: the loop it doesn't close, the learning it hasn't tested ("Whether learned associations improve prediction in bet three sixty fly is a separate research question that has not yet been tested"). The tour is a way of not sitting with the null result.

The convergence paragraph reads as recruiting copy, not narrative: "A small team can now move across neuroscience, simulation, and software engineering at a pace that would have required a much larger group a few years ago."

## Does the ending earn its claims

No, and the gap is structural.

The premise is *measured, not chosen* — "If a neural network you train is an architecture you chose, a connectome is an architecture you inherited from a real animal." But the script never runs the one control that would make that premise mean anything: the same pipeline on a shuffled or degree-matched random graph. Without it, I have no reason to believe the fly's *specific* wiring contributed anything over an arbitrary fixed nonlinear projection with a fitted readout on top. Parity with the baseline is exactly what you'd expect from a reservoir doing nothing. That isn't a nitpick — it's the central claim going unsupported.

Then the pivot:

> "That transparency is what makes the next experiment possible, and a conventional model does not offer it."

False as stated. A logistic regression on pregame stats is *more* interpretable than 167,000 nodes plus an external fitted readout. Worse: if the predictive signal lives in that readout — which parity with the baseline suggests — then tracing "which pathways carried the signal" traces something that isn't doing the work.

> "the signal is comparable to a conventional model, every step is traceable through the circuit, and the system is ready for the next intervention."

"Comparable to" is doing a lot of softening for "no better than." "Ready for the next intervention" is a claim about future work standing where a result should be, and "there is room for engineering teams to enter it" turns the close into a hiring pitch.

## What works

The dynamics section is genuinely good — the distinction between what the wiring gives you and what the modeler supplies is the clearest thing here. And "Dynamics stop being a modeling choice and start being a calibration target" is the best line in the script; it earns its abstraction.

---

**To get to APPROVE:** disclose bet365 and the commercial interest up front; add the shuffled-graph control or state plainly that the result doesn't yet distinguish the connectome from a random reservoir; benchmark 56% against something external; specify the encoding and the neuron selection; cut the JavaScript paragraph; cut or drastically compress the zebrafish/MICrONS tour; and let the ending say what it found rather than what it's ready for.
